land.text: 'the former Xia territory north of the Yellow River', which Liu Heita recovered after Dou Jiande's execution

predecessors.note: Dou Jiande's Xia ended in 621; Tang held the land until Liu Heita's rising in the fall of 621.

land.text: the former Xia territory, returned to the Tang when Liu Heita was betrayed at Rao Prefecture in spring 623

capitals.name: Mingzhou (Guangfu)
capitals.note: 'Spring 622: He claimed the title Prince of Handong and made Mingzhou (now Guangfu) his capital.' Coordinates are the researcher's reading of Guangfu (Yongnian, Handan).

rulers.name: Liu Heita (Prince of Handong)
rulers.title: Prince of Handong from spring 622
rulers.note: Infobox 'Ruler of China (Hebei)' 621-623, era Tianzao of Handong 622-623.

correction.text: Zhangnan and the former Xia core in southern Hebei (the researcher's reading of Zhangnan)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 621 (reviewer ea-04-x split). 'In fall 621, they officially rose and captured Zhangnan'; the former Xia territory was recovered only 'around the new year 622' (the 622 gain), so 621 shows the Zhangnan circle round Handan, the researcher's reading. No area figure on the page.

correction.text: the former Xia territory north of the Yellow River, with Mingzhou as capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 622-623 (reviewer ea-04-x split from the 621 keyframe). The page names Zhangnan (taken in the fall of 621), Mingzhou (the capital), Wei Prefecture (besieged 622-623) and Rao Prefecture (where he was captured) and gives the land as 'the former Xia territory north of the Yellow River'; it does not mention Luoyang or Shandong as his. Hebei is the researcher's reading; the shape alternated with the Tang's in 622. No area figure on the page.

region.text: Zhangnan and the former Xia core in southern Hebei (the researcher's reading of Zhangnan)

ledger.note: 621: Liu Heita rises. 'Former Xia officers chose Liu as leader. In fall, he took Zhangnan and rose to avenge' Dou Jiande, whom the Tang had executed.

region.text: the former Xia territory north of the Yellow River

ledger.note: 622: Liu Heita retakes the former Xia land. Around the new year 'he defeated Li Shentong, Li Yi, Li Xiaochang, and Li Shiji, and recovered the former Xia territory north of the Yellow River'; in spring he took the title Prince of Handong with Mingzhou as capital.
622: Mingzhou (now Guangfu) becomes the capital; Liu Heita claims the title Prince of Handong in spring.
622: Li Shimin drives him out. 'After a 60-plus-day stalemate on the Ming River, Li Shimin flooded his army by destroying a dam. Liu fled to the Eastern Turks, and Tang took Handong territory.'
622: he returns with Turkish troops. 'He returned with Turkish reinforcements, killed Li Daoxuan at Xiabo, and again recovered the former Xia territory within half a month.'

region.text: the former Xia territory, back to the Tang

ledger.note: 623: Liu Heita is betrayed. His forces, bogged down besieging Wei Prefecture, ran out of food; in spring (c. March 623, sources differ from January) the prefect of Rao Prefecture, Zhuge Dewei, ambushed him at a feast and handed him to Li Jiancheng; he and his brother were executed in Mingzhou's marketplace.

wars.name: Li Shimin's campaign against Liu Heita

zones.text: southern Hebei: the Ming River, Xiabo and Wei Prefecture

wars.outcome: Tang victory: Li Shimin broke Liu on the Ming River in 622; he returned with Eastern Turkish help and was destroyed at Wei Prefecture and Rao Prefecture by Li Jiancheng and Li Yuanji in early 623.

certainty.note: Rebel zone moving between Tang and rebel hands; no frontier on the page.

sources.title: Liu Heita
sources.note: Rising in fall 621, the Prince of Handong title in spring 622, the Ming River, return with Turkish aid, Wei Prefecture, capture in spring 623.

notes: Written for ea-04-x (listed by ea-03-f and the Tang dossier as 'Liu Heita (Handong)'; no Cliopatria row). The Tang dossier's 622 loss and 623 gain agree with the 622 gain and 623 dissolve here, but the Tang ledger has no 622 retaking by Li Shimin and re-loss. The page's date of the capture is c. March 623 with sources differing from January; the year is safe. Hebei is the researcher's reading of 'the former Xia territory north of the Yellow River'. Eastern Turks appear only in the war.
